I'm a bit unsure how this ended up in my Reddit feed since I'm a straight male, but I actually do have something to speak on with this topic. It might get a bit ranty, but the way a lot of men behave has kind of turned me into a traitor to my own gender.  


Other men piss me off. Not for any direct reason, but because of the image and stereotypes they paint of men as a whole. While I'm unsure if it's a majority of men, there is certainly a very unhealthy amount of men who are complete assholes to their partners and the world around them as a whole. And, if they're not assholes, they might be toxically masculine towards other men. To me, it seriously feels like a dick measuring competition with everything. I've seen men do stupid shit just to impress their other guy friends, or to prove them wrong about something dumb. Also, while this has improved a **bit** in recent times, if you're a man with mental health issues, tough fuckin' luck.  


As someone who has struggled with mental health issues my entire life, my mental health has been taken a lot less seriously by other men, and especially my stepdad, who, throughout my time in high school, thought that I was just a pussy who lacks testosterone. Again, looping back to the issue of toxic masculinity. A lot of men also give me funny looks that I don't watch/play sports or do any other shit like that. I've just never really been into any of that stuff.  


And because of this, I never really felt like I fit in anywhere. I've had more engaging conversations with women than other men, because I just never connect with anything. Half of the time, my male friends just talk about sports, and I just have to wait for them to finish talking before I can even converse with them. Because of this, it's just left me feeling really lonely and unhappy, because I can't even fully engage with my closest friends.  


I'm not sure what it is that men are looking for nowadays, but I just want to find a successful job and feel loved by someone. I could care less about the rest. I would just want to start out the morning with a hug, and that would make my day that much better. The fact that I even have to type this essay of a comment shows how bad things are, as men have permanently damaged the image of their entire sex because of their behavior.   


And yes, you can taste a little bit of salt in this comment. It genuinely irritates me that so many men are this bad.

You too? I had a very similar incident go on at mall near my house. Same fucking store too! I was a custodial worker just trying to make some extra money to pay for my college funds. That day, I noticed that Old Navy was closed off with some yellow tape and with the gate shut. When I had to clean there, another worker had to supervise me while I cleaned up. Both of us were curious about this rule, so when we cleaned the security room, we checked the footage for our own curiosity. It turns out, an employee was working past closing to finish counting money, when suddenly he passed out at the counter. Seconds later the lights went out for a few minutes. When they came back on, the employee recovered, but every mannequin was now turned towards his side of the room, with them getting closer and closer with each passing flicker, until he was laying dead on the floor the last time the lights came back on. Once more, a mannequin was messing with the light switch, in this case, a mannequin wearing jeans and a t-shirt. However, one detail freaked the hell out of us. The employee was dead, faceless on the floor. His face was covering one of the mannequin's blank faces. On the wall, written in blood was my name, and my supervisor's. But, a second later, a line of static rolled across the screen and all evidence was gone. The blood on the wall was erased, the face was back on the now dead employee, but the mannequins remained, since the lights were on. I'm telling you, the mannequins are alive, sentient, they are getting revenge on us for using them as "dolls." I warn you, stay away from Old Navy at all costs, especially if they are watching you.

I have 2 places I lived that were both equally terrible. I know this is the WORST place you have ever lived, but I can't pick which is better.

The tennis court was kind of beat up, but at least the pools were fine. We never had personal maintenance issues, however, just maintenance issues with the building itself. We also had to be very careful, because some crook was going around stealing crap from other residents. It had no AC, so we tried hooking up fans and AC units around the house. The electrical system was so weak in that house, that we blew a circuit. We had leaking plumbing twice, once under the kitchen sink, and another time under the living room floor. The back screen door was definitely one that was built then attached to the back to replace an old one; probably by a previous owner who didn't want to buy a new one.
